title: Run-rate hiring thresholds and token pricing scenarios (working sheet)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet models short-term run-rate sensitivity for hosted API token costs, maps those costs to headcount hiring triggers for both SRE/Infra and Revenue-facing roles, and proposes explicit governance thresholds for pricing and staffing actions. The goal is a compact, operational playbook that finance, product, and infra can use to make consistent decisions when token/unit costs or demand shift rapidly.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We model 3 demand scenarios (Slow, Base, Upside) and 3 price scenarios (Current baseline, +20% token price, -15% token price via optimization).
- For each scenario we estimate monthly platform token spend, gross margin impact, and the incremental HC headroom required to sustain target SLAs (p95 latency, error budget).
- We surface 3 operational triggers: Margin trigger (adjust pricing or promos), Capacity trigger (spin up Dedicated bursts / reserve), and Hiring trigger (open roles or pause).

Assumptions (key):
- Baseline monthly active tokens consumed (hosted API + dedicated ingress): 2.1B tokens/month at baseline (May 2026 observed).
- Baseline blended token cost to Redwood (infrastructure + model licensing + overhead): $0.0035 per 1k tokens (i.e., $3.5 per M). This is a blended internal cost that includes GPU run-time, networking, and amortized infra.
- Average revenue (price to customer) per 1k tokens: $0.012 (i.e., $12 per M) in current pricing mix across product tiers.
- Target gross margin floor for hosted product: 55% (finance target).
- Productivity & capacity mapping: each infra SRE/infra engineer (on-call + infra ops) supports ~120M tokens/month at base quantization and batching profiles. Each infra hire reduces observed p95 latency risk by 10% for the monitored tenant cohort.
- Revenue-facing roles (account managers/solutions) revenue efficiency: one AM effectively supports $400k MRR of committed usage; hiring gating applies once committed MRR forecast crosses $350k/AM.

Model tables (CSV style rows for paste into a sheet):
Header row:
Scenario,MonthlyTokens(M),TokenCostPerM($),TokenCostMonthly($),RevenuePerM($),RevenueMonthly($),GrossMargin($),GrossMarginPct(%),InfraHCNeeded(#),AM_HC_Needed(#)
Rows:
Slow,1200,3.5,4200,12,14400,10200,70.0,10,3
Base,2100,3.5,7350,12,25200,17850,70.8,18,5
Upside,3200,3.5,11200,12,38400,27200,70.8,27,9
Base_plus20pct_price,2100,3.5,7350,14.4,30240,22890,75.8,18,5
Base_minus15pct_cost,2100,2.975,6248,12,25200,18952,75.2,16,5
Upside_minus15pct_cost,3200,2.975,9520,12,38400,28880,76.0,24,9

Notes on table: TokenCostMonthly and RevenueMonthly are calculated as (MonthlyTokens/1M) * respective per-M prices. GrossMargin = RevenueMonthly - TokenCostMonthly; GrossMarginPct = GrossMargin/RevenueMonthly*100. InfraHCNeeded = round((MonthlyTokens / 120) ) where denominator is in M tokens per infra hire. AM_HC_Needed = round(RevenueMonthly / 400000) (MRR proxy; using revenue/12 to approximate MRR is simplified — flagged below).

Sensitivity sweeps (quick):
- If blended token cost increases by +20% (cost per M = $4.20), Base scenario gross margin drops from ~70.8% to ~64.9% (gap to target 55% still ok but narrower).
- If price erosion occurs (avg revenue per M falls to $10), Base scenario margin falls to ~65.3%.
- Optimization levers (quantization, KV caching, model routing) estimated to reduce token cost by 10–25% depending on workload.

Hiring triggers (proposed):
1) Infra hiring open (sre/infra): trigger when projected monthly tokens consistently exceed (120M * current headcount + 25% safety buffer) for 2 consecutive months OR when p95 latency degradation > 25% vs baseline for >72 hours.
2) AM hiring open (revenue): trigger when committed ARR forecast implies >350k MRR per AM required for next 90 days (i.e., revenue ramp planning shows >350k/AM).
3) Hiring pause: if gross margin on product falls below 50% and not recoverable within a 30-day action plan (pricing or cost optimization), pause all non-critical hiring approvals in product/ops.

Operational actions tied to pricing sensitivity (playbook):
- Margin Trigger (GrossMarginPct < 60%): immediate cross-functional huddle (Finance, Product, Infra). Options: temporary price increase on high-latency tiers, prioritize cache/batching rollout, move high-cost tenants to dedicated capacity with explicit surcharge.
- Capacity Trigger (InfraHCNeeded > current hc + 2 AND projected run-rate growth > 15% MoM): authorize 8-week contractor burst or open 2 full-time requisitions (fast-track).
- Promo/Discount Trigger (RevenuePerM drops >10%): stop new discounts, require sales exceptions to be documented and routed to finance lead.

Break-even and runway impacts (micro-examples):
- Example: If Upside tokens (3.2B) materialize but no cost reduction, incremental token spend is $11,200/mo and incremental gross profit is $27,200/mo — positive net contribution after infra hires in the model, but observe that infra hires will create step fixed costs (salary + benefits ~ $250k/year fully loaded per infra hire).
- Break-even hires: For each infra hire (fully loaded $250k/year -> ~$20.8k/month), the model expects each hire to enable ~120M tokens/month incremental capacity which at base margin yields ~$1,020/month gross profit per M tokens; therefore an infra hire pays for itself if it unlocks >20M additional paying tokens/month (quick check).

Governance matrix (who owns what):
- Finance (Maya Patel): maintain monthly run-rate model; sign-off on margin triggers and hiring pauses.
- Infra (Ethan Morales): validate capacity mapping, provide monthly token per-HC telemetry and p95 latency evidence.
- GTM/RevOps (Sofia Nguyen): map committed ARR/MRR forecasts to AM headcount needs and flag ACV movements.
- Exec review cadence: Monthly finance review + ad-hoc huddle on triggers.

Open questions & flags (working list):
- The blended token cost figure needs to be decomposed: how much is pure GPU runtime vs licensing vs network? Jesse (infra cost team) to provide split.
- The AM headcount mapping uses simplified revenue to MRR conversion; RevOps should provide a deal-level run-rate model to replace the approximation.
- Need a small experiment: 10% of high-volume tenants moved to cached prefix rollout to measure real-world token reduction. Target: measure 30-day delta and update model.

Recommended next steps (30/60/90):
- 30d: Finance to validate cost decomposition and update blended per-M cost; Infra to deliver per-hire effective capacity telemetry.
- 60d: Run caching experiment; update model with delta; run sensitivity on worst-case +30% token costs.
- 90d: If upside demand is realized, execute hiring plan: 2 infra hires (fast-track) + 1 AM after signed ARR > $500k.

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (for copying into sheet cells):
- TokenCostMonthly = (MonthlyTokens / 1_000_000) * TokenCostPerM
- RevenueMonthly = (MonthlyTokens / 1_000_000) * RevenuePerM
- GrossMargin = RevenueMonthly - TokenCostMonthly
- InfraHCNeeded = ROUNDUP(MonthlyTokens / 120000000)

Change log (working):
- 2026-05-10: initial draft and scenario seeds created by Maya.
- 2026-05-18: added infra capacity mapping per discussion with Ethan.
- 2026-06-02: updated with caching -15% cost column and refined governance triggers.

Notes to reviewers: this is intended to be a concise operational sheet for quick decisioning. Prefer small, testable levers (cache, routing) ahead of broad price changes. Please comment inline with objections or missing data points (tag: @finance, @infra).
